6922.t: From γεννάω (gennắō, “I beget”) + -σις (-sĭs, verbal noun suffix). Compare simple γένεσις (génesis).

6923.t: Compare Old Armenian կամուրջ (kamurǰ, “bridge”) and Hattic 𒄩𒄠𒈬𒊒𒊀 (ḫa-am-mu-ru-waₐ /⁠ḫamuruwa, ḫammuruwa, ḫāmuruwaₐ⁠/, “beam”), with further origin unknown.

6930.t: From earlier διχθά (dĭkhthắ), from δίς (dĭ́s, “twice”). The velar derivation is unclear; compare Sanskrit द्विधा (dvidhā, “by two”), the dh of which might be found in δι-χ-θά.

6916.t: From γραφή (graphḗ, “drawing, painting, writing, a writing, description, etc.”) + -ικός (-ikós), from γράφω (gráphō).

6929.t: Furnée pointed out that the traditional derivation from *δίκ-σκος (*dík-skos), from δικεῖν (dikeîn, “to cast”) is hardly possible, because the suffix “-σκο-” is rare in nominal derivation.

6935.t: Derived from δέκα (dékă) + -άς (-ắs); compare δυάς (duás), τριάς (triás), τετράς (tetrás), χιλιάς (khiliás), μυριάς (muriás).

6967.t: PIE word *dwís Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁ ▲ Proto-Indo-European *trísinflu. Proto-Indo-European *dwísder.

6924.t: Reduplicated formation. It is often connected with grānum (“seed, kernel”) and Old High German kerno (“pit, stone”), which is formally improbable.

6959.t: From διαγράφω (dĭăgrắphō, “to mark out lines, delineate”) + -ή (-ḗ).

6952.t: From διΐστημι (dĭĭ̈́stēmĭ, “separate, stand apart”) with stem as in στάσις (stắsĭs).
